subtype: Stage 6: Trust as a track record [Observer]
passage:
Dear Santosh,
I stayed with you for three weeks, and I want to write down something I noticed before I forget. Every evening Meenal told you where she was going, and every evening she was home when she said. She called when the bus was late on Tuesday. She even texted you a photo of the library board, without being asked. These are small things. But I watched them add up, day after day. I don't think you see it, because you're looking for the next mistake. Tell her you've noticed. I saw her face when I said, "Well done for calling, beta." She lit up. Kids keep doing what gets seen.
Your brother,
Lalit

qa.q: What did Meenal text Santosh without being asked?
qa.a: She texted a photo of the library board.

qa.q: Why does Lalit think Santosh hasn't noticed Meenal's progress?
qa.a: He believes Santosh is looking for the next mistake, so the small promises kept each day go unseen.

qa.q: What does Lalit suggest Santosh do?
qa.a: Tell Meenal directly that the kept promises have been noticed, since being seen for honesty encourages more of it.

qa.q: How did Meenal react when Lalit praised her for calling?
qa.a: Her face lit up, showing how much it meant to her that someone noticed.

grounding: Shows a relative noticing a teen keep small promises for weeks and urging the parent to say so aloud, since being noticed encourages honesty.

subtype: Stage 6: Trust as a track record [Observer]
passage: "Vishal, listen to me for two minutes. Don't interrupt." Rajni set her cup down on the verandah rail. "I've been here a month. Every day, Aakash has told you where he's going. Every day, home by the time he said. Last Friday he came back early from Pratik's house because he'd promised to help me with the gas booking. And he did. He didn't forget once. You still ask him three times at the door as if he's lying. I'm telling you as your elder sister: say it out loud. 'Aakash, I've noticed.' That's all. I said it to him yesterday, and he stood up straighter. A boy who gets noticed for being honest keeps being honest."

qa.q: What did Aakash come back early to help with?
qa.a: He came back early to help Rajni with the gas booking.

qa.q: What does Aakash standing up straighter suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt proud and respected at being noticed for keeping his word.

qa.q: What exactly does Rajni ask Vishal to say?
qa.a: "Aakash, I've noticed." Just naming out loud the pattern of kept promises.

qa.q: How might Aakash feel being asked three times at the door?
qa.a: He may feel distrusted despite weeks of honesty, which could discourage him if no one notices his effort.

grounding: Shows an aunt who sees a teen keep small promises for weeks and tells the parent to name it aloud, because being noticed makes honesty likelier.
